subject: Business Models
title: Super Apps
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Super Apps.

hook.text: WeChat in China is a marketplace, bank, social network, and messaging app in one. 1.3 billion users.

buildup.text: Super apps combine multiple marketplaces into one interface: food, rides, payments, shopping, all inside one app.

discovery.text: Grab in Southeast Asia started with rides, added food, payments, and insurance. One app for daily life.

twist.text: Western super apps keep failing. Uber, PayPal, and Facebook all tried and couldn't replicate the Asian model.

climax.text: Super apps work where mobile internet leapfrogged desktop. Western users already have specialized apps.

punchline.text: One app for everything. It works in Asia but the West resists.

quiz.question: Why have Western super app attempts failed?
options: Western users already have specialized apps for each need

details.summary: Super apps combine multiple marketplace verticals, payments, and services into a single platform where users fulfill diverse needs without leaving the app..
details.whyItMatters: Super apps demonstrate how cross-category marketplace effects can create unassailable competitive advantages. A user who rides, orders food, pays bills, and banks through one app faces extreme switching costs..
takeaways: Super apps integrate multiple marketplace verticals into a single user platform
Cross-service data and network effects create extreme switching costs for users
Asian super apps like WeChat and Grab dominate markets Western platforms have not cracked

faq.question: Why have super apps flourished in Asia but not in Western markets?
faq.answer: Asian markets leapfrogged to mobile-first internet use, creating demand for all-in-one mobile solutions. Mobile payment dominance provided the foundation for expanding into adjacent services. Less established incumbent apps in each category left space for one platform to serve many needs.

faq.question: Are Western companies trying to build super apps?
faq.answer: Yes. Uber added food delivery, grocery, and freight to its ride-hailing base. PayPal and Cash App are adding shopping and crypto investing. Amazon bundles e-commerce, streaming, and delivery. But Western consumers resist consolidation, preferring specialized best-in-class apps.
